findings.summary: Admitting agy/gemini-4-hydrogen@high for code_reviewer fails end-to-end because adapters/seed/agy.yaml defines no reviewer launch profile (nor reviewer_readonly_args), so candidates.build_candidates skips the route as no-profile, adapters.build_argv raises AdapterError on launch, and candidates.declared_decision rejects --review-as/office review --as pre-checks that pass scope=None.

For a non-executor role like code_reviewer, candidates.build_candidates still populates user_allow_sizes on the dispatchable=False Hydrogen candidate even for an unsized allow while candidates.route_role omits request context/run_gear for non-adaptive roles, causing executor_slates.new_gear_size to return None and routing.route to reject the route as covering an unknown task size.

While updating the Hydrogen policy banner in _dispatch_view, the function still gates installed/has_profile checks on role == 'executor' and requires size for user_allowed, causing office route policy --role code_reviewer to hide the missing agy reviewer profile and misreport a probed user-allowed agy/gemini-4-hydrogen@high as an automatic S/M canary trial (or a normal executor route when --size is given).

The new code_reviewer admission test calls routing.route directly with a synthetic candidate dict and explicit run_gear instead of exercising candidates.route_role, candidates.build_candidates, or adapter profile lookup, leaving both the missing agy reviewer profile and the user_allow_sizes rejection untested.
